nodes.summary: Let $n$, $k$ and $d$ be natural numbers and let $[n] = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$. A family $G$ of subsets of $[n]$ is a $K(d)$-family of $k$-subsets when every member of $G$ has exactly $k$ elements and any $d$ distinct members $A_1, \dots, A_d$ of $G$ with $|A_1 \cup \dots \cup A_d| \le 2k$ have a common element.
nodes.title: $K(d)$-families

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$, $k$ and $d$ with $3 \le d \le k$ and $n \ge dk/(d - 1)$, every $K(d)$-family $G$ of $k$-subsets of $[n] = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ satisfies $|G| \le \binom{n-1}{k-1}$, and if $|G| = \binom{n-1}{k-1}$ then some element of $[n]$ lies in every member of $G$.
nodes.title: Mubayi's Erdős–Ko–Rado conjecture for $K(d)$-families holds
